alert.name: ECSServiceAlarm
alert.summary: CloudWatch alarm fired for ECS service checkout

logs: EVENT BackOff Pod/checkout-748c57d7fd-bmwck: Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-748c57d7fd-bmwck_warden-pg(<UUID_1>)
EVENT BackOff Pod/checkout-748c57d7fd-zrwc5: Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-748c57d7fd-zrwc5_warden-pg(<UUID_2>)
checkout-748c57d7fd-zrwc5/checkout 2026-09-24T12:32:01.137199848Z checkout: WARN memory pressure rising
checkout-748c57d7fd-bmwck/checkout 2026-09-24T12:31:46.140738812Z checkout: WARN memory pressure rising

root_cause.hypothesis: checkout pods OOMKilled because container memory limit (48 MiB) is grossly undersized versus app's own 900MiB cache allocation attempt, causing repeated OOM kill -> CrashLoopBackOff on both replicas. Image bump (3.12-alpine -> 3.12.7-alpine) looks incidental, not causal.
evidence: memory_limit_mib=48 vs log 'allocating 900MiB cache' — ~19x over limit
restart_count=10 with BackOff events on both pods, consistent with OOM crash loop
WARN memory pressure rising precedes allocation attempt in both pod logs
deploy only changed patch version (3.12->3.12.7) of same alpine base, low likelihood of introducing new 900MiB alloc behavior
ruled_out: crashloop_containers metric shows 0, but BackOff events + restart_count=10 indicate crash-loop behavior anyway, likely metric/label mismatch not contradicting OOM cause
image tag change as root cause — patch bump unlikely to alter memory allocation logic; more likely limit was always too low or config (memory_limit_mib=48) is misconfigured/regressed separately

proposal.reasoning: Both replicas OOMKilled: container memory_limit_mib=48 is far below app's own 900MiB cache allocation, so every restart repeats the OOM kill and crashloop regardless of pod count. No listed action edits a resource limit — restart_pods just repeats the crash, scale_up/scale_down only change replica count not per-container memory cap, and rollback_deploy targets the image bump which the hypothesis marks incidental, not the limit. Root cause is a manifest/config value (memory_limit_mib) that needs a human or IaC change to raise the limit (or fix the 900MiB cache alloc) before any restart will hold.
proposal.expected_effect: No remediation attempted; a human is paged to raise checkout's container memory limit (or fix the oversized cache allocation) so pods can start without repeated OOM kills.

reasons: Action is inert or advisory; no approval required.
